assessment_summary: Individual assignment: This assignment is in the form of an individual progress report that corresponds to a specific section of the group project. The content of this report will vary depending on the student's designated role within the project team. The report comprises 1500 (± 10%) words and associated discussions during the group consultation sessions.

Group assignment: This assessment item requires students to work within their project groups to analyse and provide recommendations for resolving a business problem of an actual client. Each project group will be expected to look for and acquire their own client, and design a technology-enabled solution that will improve a substantive business process of the client. The deliverables of the project include a 15 minute presentation and a project report of 6000 (± 10%) words.

Reflective journal: Individual, continuous, reflective journal about the student’s authentic learning experience gleaned from the group project and the in-class activities. The student will draft the reflective journal continuously in Canvas and the teaching team will ask them 4-5 ‘provocative’ questions to prompt their critical reflection throughout the semester. The final deliverable is a written reflective journal of 1500 words (± 10%).

Generative AI Strategy: By developing a clear strategy for using GenAI tools in assignment work, students will enhance their ability to leverage GenAI for tasks such as identifying literature, structuring ideas, refining text, and fact-checking while ensuring ethical and effective practices. The goal is not just to ensure academic integrity but also to reflect on how GenAI tools shape analytical and critical thinking skills. The deliverable is a 600 word (± 10%) document.
Detailed information for each assessment can be found on Canvas.

items.label: Overview paragraph 1
items.text: This capstone unit bridges the gap between theory and practice by integrating knowledge and consolidating key skills developed across the Business Information Systems major. It aims to provide students with practical experience in identifying, analysing, and solving contemporary business problems. Much of this unit is dedicated to a problem-solving, experiential approach to learning. Students ensure their career-readiness by demonstrating their ability to apply concepts, theories, frameworks, methodologies, and skills to authentic problems and challenges faced in the field of information systems.

items.label: Learning outcome 1
items.text: LO1. apply and relate information systems theories and concepts in the context of an actual business problem with societal relevance

items.label: Learning outcome 2
items.text: LO2. analyse open-ended business scenarios and evaluate the implications of information systems decisions

items.label: Learning outcome 3
items.text: LO3. apply techniques for organisational and business process analyses to resolve an actual business problem

items.label: Learning outcome 4
items.text: LO4. communicate in a professional and confident manner, both orally and in writing, with actual business professionals

items.label: Learning outcome 5
items.text: LO5. apply team management concepts and theories to effectively work in, and manage, cross-functional teams

items.label: Learning outcome 6
items.text: LO6. analyse and reflect critically on the ethical and social implications of information systems.
